newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Mir cosmonauts, new crew train for repairs.
newsitem.headline: Mir cosmonauts, new crew train for repairs.

text.p: The crew of the crippled Mir space station spent Thursday preparing for a risky spacewalk and checking tools they will need to repair power supply from a damaged module, space officials said.

"The cosmonauts on board Mir are carrying out scheduled works and are working on details of their sortie to the holed module," a mission control spokeswoman told Reuters by telephone from the town of Korolyov in the Moscow suburbs.

A fresh three-member crew, which is due to fly to Mir in August, was carrying out simulated repairs while dressed in space-suits on a full-scale Mir model placed in a giant pool at the cosmonauts' training centre, the spokeswoman added.
The cosmonauts will try to seal the hole in the scientific Spektr module when they arrive at Mir.
The spokeswoman said the current three-man crew had finished unloading vital equipment from a supply craft docked to Mir and were now reloading it with garbage and unnecessary equipment.

Mir lost up to half its electric power in a June 25 collision when another Russian cargo ship hit Mir's scientific Spektr module. A failure to beef up power supplies would threaten the future of the 11-year-old space station.
Two Russian cosmonauts currently on board, Vasiliy Tsibliyev and Alexander Lazutkin, will try to repair lost power supply from Spektr's solar arrays on July 17 or July 18.
Their U.S. colleague, British-born Michael Foale, will sit in the Soyuz escape capsule for safety during the repair work, which is expected to last up to four hours.
The spokeswoman said the crew had received a video tape with recorded simulated works that they would have to carry out inside Spektr.
They will need to attach 17 internal cables to connections inside the module. The crew had to disconnect the cables and close the hatch leading to the module after the collision.

Two Russians, Anatoly Solovyov and Pavel Vinogradov, and Frenchman Leopold Eyharts are due to arrive on Mir in August. All six will work on the station for three weeks before Lazutkin and Tsibliyev return to Earth in a Soyuz craft.
Foale will be picked up from Mir by a U.S. space shuttle in September.
